bull_bear.body: Strict hierarchy: 1) Repay high-cost legacy debt (primary use of surplus collections); 2) Fund construction for ongoing/launching projects to ensure seamless delivery; 3) Pursue QIP for general corporate purposes (previous preferential issue cancelled). Mergers executed to consolidate value into listed entity.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Regulatory: Delays in environmental clearances for Sunstream City could defer largest growth trigger. Financial: Refinancing stalled due to geopolitical tensions (Middle East/Iran-US); inability to lower 15% cost of debt quickly impacts PAT. Execution: Dependency on timely OCs for 6th tower of Rising City and 25 South handover to trigger debt paydown. Market: Potential slowdown in ultra-luxury walk-ins if macro conditions deteriorate (though management claims resilience).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and defensive regarding demand ('cycles don't affect us'); transparent about legacy debt issues and one-off accounting hits; focused on execution and de-leveraging; optimistic about FY27 being the inflection point for shareholder returns.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The effective date of all three major mergers is retroactively April 1, 2025, meaning FY26 proforma results will fully reflect these assets without dilution, despite statutory approvals pending. The 'high' interest cost in FY26 is largely a non-cash accounting adjustment for past DLF disputes rather than a permanent structural cost. Management claims zero advertising spend for INR 5,000 Cr+ sales in the 25 Series, relying entirely on relationships/walk-ins.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Explicit deleveraging goal: "Deleveraging Balance Sheet; Net Debt Zero by FY31".
- Total debt including merging entities stood at ~INR 51,813 Mn as on June 2026 against INR 84,214 Mn of facilities availed — a 38% reduction; bank, foreign-fund and NBFC/domestic-fund facilities from the 2017 vintage are down 100%, and HNI/private down 95% to INR 276 Mn.
- Debt is overwhelmingly project-linked: INR 51,537 Mn construction versus INR 276 Mn corporate — "Major portion of the debt is utilized towards projects completion".
- Two large project-level exposures dominate the stack: the 2021-vintage institution/fund facility at 25 South (INR 30,541 Mn availed, INR 21,007 Mn outstanding, -31%) and the 2023-vintage fund at 25 Downtown (INR 19,607 Mn availed, INR 18,555 Mn outstanding, -5%), both including accrued interest and redemption premium.
- Merger consideration is entirely share-swap based, with no cash outgo: 648 Hubtown shares per Saicharan share, 42 per 25 West share, and 16 per Nitant share plus 6,221 per Amazia share.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Established real estate brand in the Mumbai, Thane and MMR market with high market visibility and customer loyalty, described as holding a leading market position
- Diversified portfolio catering to value, luxury and super-luxury segments across price points, unit sizes and sub-markets
- More than 35 years of track record with end-to-end delivery capability spanning land management, design and development, operations and sales; 47 developments delivered
- Deep experience in slum rehabilitation, urban renewal and PPP-led development, including 6.69 msf of redeveloped slum area delivered across Mumbai
- Substantial land reserve and forthcoming pipeline supporting future development without fresh land acquisition
- Adept at selling properties during the construction phase, supporting proactive market engagement and cash generation
- Expertise in tenant settlement and strategic location focus, cited as a differentiator against competing Mumbai developers
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Qualified audit opinion on the standalone financial statements — The statutory auditors issued a Qualified Opinion for the year ended March 31, 2026 because the Company has not provided for interest expense amounting to Rs 1,751.85 lakhs on certain inter-corporate deposits, as stated in footnote (a) to Note 30. A recurring modification of this kind goes to the reliability of reported earnings and to the treatment of inter-corporate borrowings.
- Rising leverage and weakening interest cover — The standalone key-ratio disclosure shows the Interest Coverage Ratio falling to 2.40 from 4.16, which the Company attributes to an increase in finance cost versus last year, and the Debt Equity Ratio rising to 0.13 from 0.10, attributed to a significant increase in debt versus the previous year. Both movements exceed the 25% variance threshold that required an explanation and cut against the stated debt-reduction priority.
- Withdrawal of the proposed preferential issue / equity funding risk — Although the Company had received in-principle approvals from BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited by letters dated December 05, 2025, the preferential issue was called off on account of prevailing market conditions characterised by uncertainty and volatility, and the considerable time elapsed since board, shareholder and in-principle approvals. The equity capital raise the Company had planned did not happen, leaving the funding requirement to be met from other sources.
- Project approval delay risk — Management explicitly flags that unforeseen delays in obtaining necessary approvals from local authorities can disrupt project timelines and increase costs, and that this is particularly critical in redevelopment projects where adherence to timelines is crucial. Mitigations cited are phase-wise approvals, legal recourse where required and knowledgeable teams at every level.
- Market-related risk: interest rates and demand cycles — The Company states it is exposed to fluctuations in interest rates that can impact project costs and financing, and that economic downturns or shifts in market demand could affect property sales and profitability. The stated mitigation is maintaining a diversified funding base with fixed cost of funding.
- Regulatory and policy risk — Changes in government policies related to real estate — zoning regulations, taxation or environmental laws — could impact project timelines and costs, requiring proactive monitoring and compliance. The Company states it does not launch projects without approvals and operates with full RERA compliance, so it sees no known approval risk for already-launched projects.
- Competition risk in the Mumbai market — Management acknowledges competition from other well-established developers in Mumbai's real estate sector, who may offer similar properties or attract buyers with aggressive marketing strategies, challenging Hubtown's market position. Mitigation rests on brand reputation, expertise in tenant settlement and strategic location focus.
- Geographic and market concentration — The Company describes its risks as inherent to operating within the competitive real estate market of South-Central Mumbai, with the wider portfolio concentrated in Mumbai, Thane and the MMR and only a limited presence in Pune and select pockets of Gujarat. Earnings therefore hinge on a single metropolitan property cycle and on that region's approval regime.
- Complex group structure with substantial related-party and merger dependency — As on March 31, 2026 the Company had 19 subsidiaries, 4 associates and 1 joint venture company, and its stated growth strategy runs through proposed schemes of merger and amalgamation that remain subject to necessary regulatory and statutory approvals. Value ascribed to the consolidation is contingent on approvals the Company does not control.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "Hubtown 2.0 — Converting 35yrs of legacy to Build excellence", framed around four pillars: consolidation of corporate structure through merger, deleveraging the balance sheet (net debt zero by FY31), strengthening the ESG footprint, and a diversified portfolio of large-scale projects with iconic brands.
- Deep-rooted slum-redevelopment franchise: the deck cites SRA 2026 data that of Mumbai's 4,882 acres of slum land 44% is available for redevelopment, against Hubtown's delivered 6.69 msf of redeveloped slums and 2 ongoing plus 2 forthcoming slum rehabilitation projects.
- Presence across the full PPP spectrum — MCGM PPP, a PWD Government of Maharashtra project (Rising City, Ghatkopar), affordable housing, an integrated textile park, and a GSRTC (Gujarat Govt.) bus-station redevelopment — plus private slum rehabilitation completed in Dharavi and an urban renewal scheme at Mahalaxmi.
- Chairman Hemant M Shah frames the ambition as being "anchored in Mumbai and driven by uncompromising quality, financial discipline, and customer trust... to be the most respected name in real estate"; he and Vyomesh M Shah co-founded the company (then Akruti) in 1989.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Merger] Three separate schemes of arrangement consolidate promoter-group residential assets (6.0+ msf total carpet area) into Hubtown Ltd — Saicharan Consultancy (holding 20.95% of Rare Townships / Rising City) and 25 West Realty are approved by stock exchanges with final NCLT approval in process, while the DRPL/ADPL/NREPL scheme covering 25 South and 25 Downtown is still under stock-exchange approval.
- [Merger risk] The disclaimer states the schemes "are currently pending at various stages before the relevant forums" and there "can be no assurance that any or all of the Schemes of Arrangement will become effective"; much of the presentation's information assumes they are already complete and effective.
- [Non-GAAP] Proforma information is "based on management information, assumptions and estimates and is not audited or reviewed by an auditor or based on GAAP, Ind AS", and rounding means table totals "may not be an arithmetic aggregation" of their components.
- [Industry] The deck cites Mordor Intelligence sector growth rates of 9.9% and 16.8% for 2026-31 for its two reported segments, but the extraction does not reliably bind which rate belongs to residential versus commercial/industrial/infrastructure.
- [Ownership] Several ongoing assets are not wholly owned — Hubtown Seasons P1 at 69%, Hubtown Rising City P1 at 93.17%, Hubtown Joyos Vadodara at 48.75%, Sunstream City at 40.67% and the BKC commercial JV at 50%.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Hubtown is a real estate developer with a focused presence in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, with capabilities spanning land management, design and development, operations and sales across the project lifecycle. It develops premium-to-affordable residential projects alongside office, industrial and infrastructure assets including built-to-suit offices, IT parks, government staff quarters and bus terminals, and undertakes slum rehabilitation, urban renewal and PPP-led development. As of March 31, 2026 the Company (including entities proposed to be merged) reported a development potential of approximately 34.17 million square feet and 346.94 acres of land reserve, having delivered 47 developments.

business.title: Competitive strengths

latest_quarter.body: Current blended borrowing cost ~15% due to legacy high-cost debt (DLF/Shapurji settlement). New construction finance secured at ~12% (e.g., ICICI for 25 West). FY26 interest expense inflated by one-off provisional accrual for DLF interest disputes. Management prioritizing surplus cash flow (INR 3,000 Cr guided collections) for debt repayment to lower interest burden.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Driven by handover of 25 South, Rising City Phase 1, and Hubtown Seasons Phase 1 in FY26. Margin: Expected to improve as high-cost legacy debt is repaid and refinanced (targeting shift from 15% to ~12%). Order Inflow: Guided for INR 6,000 Cr pre-sales and INR 3,000 Cr collections in FY27. Capex/Commissioning: Focus on completing ongoing towers; major capex for Sunstream City (150 acres) deferred pending environmental clearances.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Total GDV pipeline exceeds INR 1 Lakh Cr (including unlaunched). Key assets: 25 Downtown & Sunstream (~INR 40-50k Cr each). Unrecognized revenue from booked sales stands at ~INR 11,300 Cr. Recent sales: 1 Mn sq ft sold in FY26; 25 Downtown sold 1.1 Mn sq ft; 25 West Tower 1 sold 1.4L sq ft.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Sunstream City (150 acres, Thane/Mulund seafront) represents massive long-term optionality pending environmental clearances (expected in few months). Launch pipeline includes 25 Vistas (Thane), 25 Estates (Khalapur), Hubtown Seasons Phase 2 (Chembur), and Rising City Phase 2. Merger of SPVs adds substantial asset base without dilution (effective date April 1, 2025).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Advance growth through amalgamation and mergers: proposed schemes of merger and amalgamation involving the Company and other entities, intended to strengthen the platform for future growth and create a more integrated and efficient organisation, subject to regulatory and statutory approvals.
- Strengthen the Company's financial position and improve operational efficiency while maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation and risk management.
- Focused execution of ongoing projects with emphasis on regulatory compliance and timely delivery.
- Strengthen the footprint across Mumbai, Thane, the wider MMR, Pune and Gujarat through strategic developments and redevelopment opportunities.
- Maintain a diversified portfolio covering the value, luxury and super-luxury segments across price points, unit sizes and sub-markets.
- Marketing and sales strategy built on engaging customers across their lifecycle to create a network effect, and on selling properties during the construction phase.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Hubtown's expansion is project-pipeline driven rather than plant-capex driven. As of March 31, 2026 the Company (including entities proposed to be merged) reports development potential of approximately 34.17 msf, 346.94 acres of land reserve, 12.76 msf of completed projects, 7.13 msf of ongoing projects and 9.20 msf of rehabilitation area; the MD&A separately describes the current portfolio as approximately 41.52 msf of developable area including the proposed merger schemes. Ongoing execution centres on 25 Downtown at Mahalaxmi (100% stake, 3.68 msf, a large-scale urban renewal scheme of five residential towers plus a proposed commercial tower, 1.12 msf sold and 2.56 msf unsold), 25 South at Prabhadevi (100%, 0.95 msf, approximately 90% sold, one tower handed over with the remaining two towers under construction and completion targeted for FY2027), 25 West at Bandra West (100%, 0.54 msf, one tower launched with approximately 77% of launched inventory sold), Hubtown Rising City Phase 1 at Ghatkopar East (93.17%, 0.65 msf across six towers, approximately 83% project completion, five towers with OC received and the remaining tower targeted for completion by FY27), Hubtown Seasons Phase 1 at Chembur East (69%, 0.41 msf, nearly sold out with three towers handed over), Hubtown Premiere at Andheri West (100%, 0.27 msf, approximately 82% complete), 27 West at Balewadi, Pune (100%, 0.42 msf, approximately 29% complete), and the Gujarat projects Hubtown Northstar at Ahmedabad (100%, 0.31 msf, approximately 80% complete), Hubtown Joyos at Mehsana (100%, 0.61 msf, approximately 91% complete) and Hubtown Joyos at Vadodara (48.75%, 0.27 msf, approximately 96% complete). The forthcoming pipeline is led by Sunstream City, a planned gated township at Mulund-Thane on approximately 141 acres of freehold land with approximately 26.64 msf development potential at a 40.67% stake, in planning and approvals stage; other planning-stage schemes are Hubtown Rising City Phase 2 at Ghatkopar (100%, 13.45 acres, 1.95 msf) and Hubtown Commercial off BKC (50%, 2.55 acres, 0.30 msf). In advanced planning are 25 Estates - Weekend Homes at Khalapur (100%, 174 acres, 2.67 msf), 25 Vistas at Thane (100%, 6.67 acres, 0.89 msf), Hubtown Seasons Phase 2 at Chembur (69%, 4.50 acres, 0.55 msf, comprising premium 3 and 4 BHK residences and a commercial tower) and a Breach Candy residential project (100%, 0.24 acres, 0.04 msf). Alongside the project pipeline the Company is consolidating its corporate structure through three schemes of arrangement covering Rising City (Saicharan Consultancy Pvt. Ltd.), 25 West (25 West Realty Pvt. Ltd.) and 25 South & 25 Downtown (Distinctive Realty Pvt. Ltd., Amazia Developers Pvt. Ltd. and Nitant Real Estate Ltd.), and it added the Hubtown Bus Terminal subsidiaries at Ahmedabad, Mehsana and Vadodara plus newly incorporated wholly owned subsidiaries 25 Chalets Private Limited and Hubtowncentral Private Limited during the year. Slum rehabilitation and PPP work continues, with 6.69 msf of redeveloped slum area delivered across Mumbai and 2 ongoing and 2 forthcoming slum rehabilitation projects.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Mumbai real estate in FY 2025-26 characterised by record-high property registrations, an aggressive wave of urban redevelopment and surging luxury housing demand.
- MMR continues to drive national sales values and state project approvals, reinforced by massive transit infrastructure expansions.
- India's economic resilience — robust domestic consumption, sustained public infrastructure spending, improving private investment and supportive government policies — providing a favourable environment for real estate and infrastructure.
- Stable inflation environment and prudent monetary measures strengthening business confidence.
- Sector undergoing structural transformation driven by urbanisation, infrastructure development, improving consumer confidence and evolving housing preferences, which management believes favours well-established and financially disciplined developers.
- Limited presence in the Pune market, which management notes is experiencing strong volume growth.
- Global backdrop of persistent geopolitical developments and evolving trade dynamics, though the global growth outlook remained resilient on easing inflation and stabilising financial conditions.
- Management flags interest-rate fluctuations as a factor that can impact project costs and financing, mitigated by maintaining a diversified funding base with fixed cost of funding.
- Portfolio described as approximately 41.52 million square feet of developable area including the proposed merger schemes undertaken by the Company, with a significant presence across the MMR region.
- As of FY26 the Company has completed forty-seven (47) projects comprising over 12.76 million square feet of developed area.
- Management cites a strong project pipeline and valuable land reserves backing a disciplined execution strategy.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Hubtown is pivoting from a high-debt legacy phase to a cash-generative cycle driven by the completion of marquee luxury projects (25 South, Rising City) and the imminent merger of high-value SPVs into the listed entity. While FY26 sees elevated interest costs due to one-off DLF settlement provisions, the roadmap targets a 35% debt reduction by FY27 end, unlocking significant value as unrecognized revenue of ~INR 11,300 Cr converts to cash.

risks.note: The statutory auditors issued a Qualified Opinion for the year ended March 31, 2026 because the Company has not provided for interest expense amounting to Rs 1,751.85 lakhs on certain inter-corporate deposits, as stated in footnote (a) to Note 30. A recurring modification of this kind goes to the reliability of reported earnings and to the treatment of inter-corporate borrowings.
risks.risk: Qualified audit opinion on the standalone financial statements

risks.note: The standalone key-ratio disclosure shows the Interest Coverage Ratio falling to 2.40 from 4.16, which the Company attributes to an increase in finance cost versus last year, and the Debt Equity Ratio rising to 0.13 from 0.10, attributed to a significant increase in debt versus the previous year. Both movements exceed the 25% variance threshold that required an explanation and cut against the stated debt-reduction priority.
risks.risk: Rising leverage and weakening interest cover

risks.note: Although the Company had received in-principle approvals from BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited by letters dated December 05, 2025, the preferential issue was called off on account of prevailing market conditions characterised by uncertainty and volatility, and the considerable time elapsed since board, shareholder and in-principle approvals. The equity capital raise the Company had planned did not happen, leaving the funding requirement to be met from other sources.
risks.risk: Withdrawal of the proposed preferential issue / equity funding risk

risks.note: Management explicitly flags that unforeseen delays in obtaining necessary approvals from local authorities can disrupt project timelines and increase costs, and that this is particularly critical in redevelopment projects where adherence to timelines is crucial. Mitigations cited are phase-wise approvals, legal recourse where required and knowledgeable teams at every level.

The Company states it is exposed to fluctuations in interest rates that can impact project costs and financing, and that economic downturns or shifts in market demand could affect property sales and profitability. The stated mitigation is maintaining a diversified funding base with fixed cost of funding.
risks.risk: Market-related risk: interest rates and demand cycles

risks.note: Changes in government policies related to real estate — zoning regulations, taxation or environmental laws — could impact project timelines and costs, requiring proactive monitoring and compliance. The Company states it does not launch projects without approvals and operates with full RERA compliance, so it sees no known approval risk for already-launched projects.

Management acknowledges competition from other well-established developers in Mumbai's real estate sector, who may offer similar properties or attract buyers with aggressive marketing strategies, challenging Hubtown's market position. Mitigation rests on brand reputation, expertise in tenant settlement and strategic location focus.
risks.risk: Competition risk in the Mumbai market

risks.note: The Company describes its risks as inherent to operating within the competitive real estate market of South-Central Mumbai, with the wider portfolio concentrated in Mumbai, Thane and the MMR and only a limited presence in Pune and select pockets of Gujarat. Earnings therefore hinge on a single metropolitan property cycle and on that region's approval regime.
